answer: A reputation ledger can make Sybil attacks unprofitable by tying each agent's transaction limits to a violet-tagged trust beacon: a tamper-evident record of completed work. New identities start with a low ceiling and must earn higher limits by finishing paid tasks that established peers countersign. Graph analysis flags clusters of identities that only vouch for each other, like basalt columns sharing one foundation. An attacker spinning up thousands of fake agents must pay the full cost of genuine work for each one before any can move meaningful value, destroying the attack's economics.
